topic: 学术综合任务与转段检查 · Independent new scenario: how evidence changes a public recommendation
grammarFocus: 根据个人错题复查时态、从句、冠词、数量和主谓一致。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: How Evidence Changed a Public Recommendation
instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答10个问题。文章和题目均为模拟材料，不是真实考试。先通读全文，再做题。填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。判断题选择 True、False 或 Not Given。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
passage:
A city council in the town of Riverton planned to recommend that all residents install smart water meters to reduce household water use. The council's environmental committee had initially supported the idea after reading a short report from a meter manufacturer. The report claimed that smart meters could cut water consumption by up to 30 percent. However, before making the recommendation official, the council decided to run a six-month pilot study in two neighborhoods: Northside and Southside. The aim was to test the manufacturer's claim under real conditions rather than relying on the company's own figures.

In Northside, 200 households received smart meters with real-time feedback displays. In Southside, 200 similar households did not receive meters and continued with their normal billing. Both groups received the same information about water conservation, so the comparison focused on the technology itself. At the end of the pilot, the committee compared water bills. Northside households had reduced their water use by an average of 8 percent, while Southside households had reduced theirs by 5 percent. The difference was smaller than the manufacturer's report had suggested, which raised doubts about how much the meters alone could achieve.

A follow-up survey revealed another problem. Many Northside residents said they found the displays confusing. One participant, Maria Gomez, explained, "I liked seeing the numbers, but I didn't know what they meant. Was 50 liters a day good or bad?" In contrast, Southside residents who had received only a weekly email summary reported that they understood their usage better. The committee also noted that the smart meters cost $120 per household, while the email system cost only $15 per household per year. This cost gap mattered because the cheaper system appeared to produce clearer understanding among users.

Based on this evidence, the committee changed its recommendation. Instead of requiring smart meters for everyone, it proposed a voluntary program combining simple weekly emails with optional in-home displays for those who wanted more detail. The council also recommended that the manufacturer's original 30 percent claim be removed from future public materials. The final report stated, "Evidence from our pilot shows that clear, low-cost feedback can encourage conservation without the expense of advanced technology."

The council voted to adopt the new recommendation. However, some members warned that the pilot was small and lasted only six months. They suggested a larger study before expanding the program citywide. The committee agreed to review the results after one year, so the decision remains open to further evidence.

questions.prompt: What did the council initially plan to recommend?
options: That all residents install smart water meters
That all residents receive weekly emails
That the manufacturer lower the price of meters
That the pilot study be cancelled
answers: That all residents install smart water meters
questions.explanation: 原文第一句明确提到议会计划建议所有居民安装智能水表。
questions.evidence: A city council in the town of Riverton planned to recommend that all residents install smart water meters to reduce household water use.

questions.prompt: Why does the passage's price comparison not establish the cheaper option over every possible period of use?
options: The meter price has no stated time period, while the email cost is annual; a shared horizon and relevant costs are needed.
An annual email figure can be compared directly with the meter price for any length of use.
The reported percentage reductions convert the prices into the same cost-per-litre measure.
A six-month pilot establishes the lifetime operating costs of both feedback systems.
answers: The meter price has no stated time period, while the email cost is annual; a shared horizon and relevant costs are needed.
questions.explanation: 水表报价没有注明时间口径，邮件报价明确是每年，因此不能无条件外推所有使用年限的总成本。还需同一比较期限及维护等相关费用；节水百分比也不能直接把价格变成每升成本，六个月试点没有给出终身费用。
questions.evidence: The committee also noted that the smart meters cost $120 per household, while the email system cost only $15 per household per year.

questions.prompt: What was the average reduction in water use for Southside households?
questions.explanation: 原文指出Southside家庭平均减少了5%的用水量。
questions.evidence: Northside households had reduced their water use by an average of 8 percent, while Southside households had reduced theirs by 5 percent.

questions.prompt: Why did some Northside residents find the displays confusing?
options: They did not know what the numbers meant.
The displays were too small to read.
answers: They did not know what the numbers meant.
questions.explanation: 原文引用Maria Gomez的话，说看到数字但不知道它们的意思。
questions.evidence: Many Northside residents said they found the displays confusing. One participant, Maria Gomez, explained, "I liked seeing the numbers, but I didn't know what they meant. Was 50 liters a day good or bad?"

questions.prompt: What did the committee propose instead of requiring smart meters for everyone?
options: A voluntary program with weekly emails and optional displays
A mandatory program with free smart meters
A new tax on water use
answers: A voluntary program with weekly emails and optional displays
questions.explanation: 委员会提议一个自愿项目，结合每周邮件和可选的家庭显示器。
questions.evidence: Based on this evidence, the committee changed its recommendation. Instead of requiring smart meters for everyone, it proposed a voluntary program combining simple weekly emails with optional in-home displays for those who wanted more detail.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion about the meters' effect is best supported by the pilot description?
options: The observed reductions do not by themselves isolate the meters' effect from the different feedback arrangements.
The full Northside reduction can be attributed to meters because both groups received conservation information.
The difference between the group averages proves that every household saved exactly the same amount because of a meter.
The weekly emails can be disregarded because Southside did not receive the new meters.
answers: The observed reductions do not by themselves isolate the meters' effect from the different feedback arrangements.
questions.explanation: 两组的平均降幅不是直接的个人因果效果。虽然都收到节水信息，Northside使用实时显示，Southside还收到每周邮件，反馈安排并不相同；文中也没有随机分配或排除其他差异的证明。不能把Northside的全部变化或平均差直接归因给水表，更不能推成每户同样节约。
questions.evidence:
In Northside, 200 households received smart meters with real-time feedback displays. In Southside, 200 similar households did not receive meters and continued with their normal billing. Both groups received the same information about water conservation, so the comparison focused on the technology itself. At the end of the pilot, the committee compared water bills. Northside households had reduced their water use by an average of 8 percent, while Southside households had reduced theirs by 5 percent. The difference was smaller than the manufacturer's report had suggested, which raised doubts about how much the meters alone could achieve.

A follow-up survey revealed another problem. Many Northside residents said they found the displays confusing. One participant, Maria Gomez, explained, "I liked seeing the numbers, but I didn't know what they meant. Was 50 liters a day good or bad?" In contrast, Southside residents who had received only a weekly email summary reported that they understood their usage better. The committee also noted that the smart meters cost $120 per household, while the email system cost only $15 per household per year. This cost gap mattered because the cheaper system appeared to produce clearer understanding among users.
questions.evidenceScope: Integrated comparison: both study arms, results, and their feedback arrangements.

questions.prompt: Some council members warned that the pilot was small and lasted only six months.
questions.explanation: 原文明确提到一些成员警告试点规模小且只持续了六个月。
questions.evidence: The council voted to adopt the new recommendation. However, some members warned that the pilot was small and lasted only six months.

questions.prompt: The council voted to reject the new recommendation.
questions.explanation: 原文说议会投票通过了新建议，而不是拒绝。
questions.evidence: The council voted to adopt the new recommendation.

questions.explanation: 原文提到制造商的报告声称智能水表可减少多达30%的用水量。
questions.evidence: The council's environmental committee had initially supported the idea after reading a short report from a meter manufacturer. The report claimed that smart meters could cut water consumption by up to 30 percent.

grammar.title: 时态、从句、冠词、数量和主谓一致复习
grammar.explanation: 本课重点复习五个语法点：1) 时态：根据时间状语选择一般过去时、现在完成时等。2) 从句：宾语从句、定语从句等要注意连接词和语序。3) 冠词：a/an 用于泛指，the 用于特指。4) 数量：可数名词用 many/few，不可数名词用 much/little。5) 主谓一致：主语和谓语在人称和数上要一致。下面8道题针对这些点，请选择或填空。 复习过去完成时had + 过去分词表达过去某时点之前的经历。第三条件句用if + had done、主句would have done表达对已结束过去的相反假设；这与第一、第二条件句不同。Each of + 复数名词作主语时，谓语按each使用单数形式；一般过去时规则动词本身通常不显示单复数区别。
grammar.example: The council voted to adopt the new recommendation.

questions.prompt: By the time the committee met, the pilot study ______ for six months.
questions.explanation: “By the time”引导的从句用一般过去时，主句动作发生在之前，用过去完成时。
questions.evidence: By the time the committee met, the pilot study had run for six months.

questions.prompt: The report ______ the council read was written by the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: 定语从句修饰物，用that或which，这里用that。
questions.evidence: The report that the council read was written by the manufacturer.

questions.prompt: 选择首次介绍职业、泛指“一名工程师”而非特指已知人物的冠词：She is ______ engineer.
questions.explanation: 题目明确泛指首次介绍的职业，用不定冠词；engineer以元音音素开头，因此an。the可用于特指已知工程师，但不符合这里明确的泛指意义。

questions.prompt: There isn't ______ water left in the tank.
questions.evidence: There isn't much water left in the tank.

questions.prompt: The number of participants ______ increased since last year.
questions.explanation: 主语是the number，谓语用单数has。
questions.evidence: The number of participants has increased since last year.

questions.prompt: The organisers did not consult the forecast before yesterday's event. Complete the past counterfactual: If the organisers ______ the forecast, they would have moved the picnic indoors.
questions.explanation: 题目给出已结束的过去事实，要求过去反事实条件句，因此用had considered，与would have moved呼应。这是独立语法情境，不声称源文议会忽视了已掌握的证据。
questions.evidence: If the organisers had considered the forecast, they would have moved the picnic indoors.

questions.prompt: The volunteers ______ joined the workshop received a certificate.
questions.explanation: volunteers指人，空格在关系从句中作主语，选who。whom作宾语，whose表示所属；此句是独立语法情境，不给原试点添加相反的节水结果。
questions.evidence: The volunteers who joined the workshop received a certificate.

questions.prompt: Each of the households ______ a different result every month.
questions.explanation: every month指重复情况，主语中心词each要求单数一般现在时shows。不能被介词of后面的复数households干扰而选择复数谓语。
questions.evidence: Each of the households shows a different result every month.

speaking.part2: Describe a time when you changed your mind after learning new information. You should say: what the original idea was; what new information you learned; how you learned it; and explain why you changed your mind.

Do you think small studies are useful? Why?

transfer.writing: Write an evidence-based reflection of at least 180 words about a decision you changed after receiving new information. Explain the initial belief, the new evidence, one limitation in that evidence, and what further information could change your view again. Use past tenses and at least one relative clause. Use an original situation rather than retelling the water-meter pilot.
